findings.claim: issue preclusion bars repeating a factual or legal issue already validly, finally and necessarily decided in an earlier proceeding
findings.issue: The unconditional opening omits actual litigation and limits on who may be bound. The later can matter qualifies different claims, not applicability of the bar; an unrelated litigant does not generally lose a fresh hearing solely because the issue was decided elsewhere.
findings.required_fix: State that issue preclusion can bar a party who had a full and fair opportunity to litigate an issue actually litigated and necessarily resolved in a valid final judgment. Avoid an absolute same-parties-only rule because recognized nonparty exceptions and nonmutual uses exist. Add the more explicit support to the source bundle and preserve a versioned correction.

findings.required_fix: State that issue preclusion can bar a party who had a full and fair opportunity to litigate an issue actually litigated and necessarily resolved in a valid final judgment. Avoid an absolute same-parties-only rule because recognized nonparty exceptions and nonmutual uses exist. Add the more explicit support to the source bundle and preserve a versioned correction.
